reason: planning stopped before any code was written: the plan still needed revising in the last round (round 5 of 5). I read checks.rs (refusing_check at :518, the guard at :415, check_scope_limit), fake.rs reader_turn, the producer and verifier turns, steward.rs from_change and RequestQueue, proposals.rs accept_request, code_health.rs structural_text, and the CLI drain, job_plan, steward and audience tests. The plan fits the reading, and its seams exist: the step! macro, refusing_check, base_reading/case in the corpus, from_change and accept_request. Its claims about job_plan.rs:166/169, the proposals.rs accept test, the fake reader and the index-matched fake verifier hold up. One gap blocks acceptance. The drain.rs helper `queue_steward_request` (drain.rs:2573-2601) sends its text through `RequestQueue` and `StewardRequest::from_change`. Its text has no bullets, so every queued request gets the three standard Steward bullets. About twenty drain tests use this helper with `Scenario::default()` or `rated_scenario()` readings. Neither reading covers 'fmt, clippy and test pass' (its only own stem is `clipp`) or 'The change is made as described: A repeated failure'. The new gate would refuse them and break `report.landed == 1` and similar assertions. The plan's dependents list omits these tests and wrongly says the rated_scenario tests need no change. Without that, criterion 8 cannot be shown as planned, and the fix (a per-scenario bullet or resized verdicts) is unplanned. The rest are minor: the heuristic is complex and gives the reader no up-front convention, a location citation is wrong, and the structural_text sibling-stem behaviour is untested.
